t: An 8-bit chip with built-in USB that can pretend to be a keyboard.
steps: Buy an Arduino Leonardo or a SparkFun Pro Micro from a maker shop.
Get a USB cable that fits the board. Most use micro-USB.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Plug in the board and choose Arduino Leonardo from the board menu. Pro Micro owners add the SparkFun board package first.
Open the Blink example and press Upload.
Try the Keyboard example next. The board types text into your computer.
The port can vanish after a bad upload. Press reset twice and upload again.
meta: Wild Open. From $9.95. Easy to find.
